newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville leaves next-day power prices unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville leaves next-day power prices unchanged.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) left its next day price offers unchanged after slightly lowering them Monday, the agency said Tuesday.

For Wednesday, BPA continued to offer block power during heavy-load hours at $18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) in the Northwest and $19.50 at the California-Oregon border (COB) and Nevada-Oregon border (NOB).
Off-peak firm sales for all deliveries were still offered at $15.00 per MWh.
Non-firm offers were also unchanged at $20.00 for peak California borders sales and at $18.50 for the Northwest.
BPA continued to offer non-firm power during light load hours for deliveries in the Northwest and California border at $15.00-16.00.

Market sources have attributed BPA's lower price offers this week to an abundance of hydroelectric power in the Northwest following the achievement of target reservoir levels at dams including Grand Coulee in Washington.
